overview: This batch focuses on finalizing the simulation loop by implementing deterministic state serialization for save/load integrity and optimizing the tick-based physics integration for ultra-endgame stability. These tasks close the final gaps in simulation coverage by ensuring reproducible state transitions and minimizing memory fragmentation during long-running sessions.

tasks.title: Implement Deterministic State Hashing for Save/Load Integrity
tasks.architectural_spec: Implement a zero-heap, constexpr-friendly state hasher using FNV-1a 64-bit algorithm. The serializer must traverse the component array linearly. Use std::span for contiguous memory access. No dynamic allocations during hashing. The hash must be stable across different compilation units if the struct layout is identical. Include a static_assert for struct size alignment. The implementation should fit within 40 lines of logic, focusing on the hash accumulation loop and the finalization step.
acceptance_criteria: Hash value is identical for the same state across 1000 runs.
No heap allocations occur during hashing.
Unit tests pass for edge cases (empty state, max capacity).
tasks.player_fun_impact: Ensures 100% reliable save/load functionality, preventing progress loss in long campaigns.

tasks.title: Optimize Fixed-Step Integration for Ultra-Endgame Stability
tasks.architectural_spec: Refactor the semi-implicit Euler integrator to use a fixed timestep of 1/60s. Implement a 'catch-up' loop for variable frame times using a while loop with a max iteration count of 4 to prevent spiral of death. Use float32 for all calculations to maintain cache locality. Store position and velocity in a packed struct. The logic should handle the accumulation of delta time and the step execution in under 50 lines. Ensure no floating-point drift by resetting the accumulator modulo the fixed step.
acceptance_criteria: Physics simulation remains stable at 10,000+ ticks.
No visible jitter in object movement.
Memory usage for physics state remains constant.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Provides smooth, predictable motion for all entities, enhancing the visual clarity of the simulation.

tasks.title: Compact Event Log Buffer for Long-Running Sessions
tasks.architectural_spec: Implement a circular buffer for the event log with a fixed capacity of 1024 entries. Use a struct with a 32-bit timestamp and a 16-bit event ID. The push operation should overwrite the oldest entry when full. Provide a method to retrieve the last N events using a simple index calculation. The implementation should be header-only if possible, or split into a minimal .cpp file. Total logic lines should not exceed 30. Ensure thread-safety is not required as the simulation is single-threaded.
acceptance_criteria: Memory footprint of the event log is constant.
Retrieval of the last 10 events is O(1).
No memory leaks detected in Valgrind.
Log entries are correctly ordered by timestamp.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Reduces memory usage in long campaigns, allowing for more complex entity counts without performance degradation.
